config.system_prompt: You are a helpful assistant built from raw HTTP calls in Chapter 1 of The Art of Building AI Coding Agents. Answer briefly.

tools.name: agent_status
tools.description: Report the selected model, last response and session token counts, cache hit rate and derived session USD cost (unknown when prices are unavailable).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read text with one-based inclusive start_line/end_line. Optional max_bytes bounds the read; job reports cap inline output and preserve the full result on disk.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List immediate entries, sorted by name; directories end with /.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search files recursively using a regular expression. context_lines defaults to zero. Output uses grep path:line:text and path-line-context with merged windows.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write text, creating parent directories. Existing files require overwrite:true unless append:true. Append preserves existing content.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace one exact, unique old_text anchor with new_text. Zero or multiple matches refuse without changing the file; read and provide a more specific anchor.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Start a fresh /bin/sh in a PTY. cwd applies only to this call, relative to the workspace. Merged output and exit_code stay on disk; a running report is a handle, not cancellation. ai_callback_delay is seconds (default 3); pattern matches unseen output; max_output_bytes defaults to 16384.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: wait_for_job
tools.description: Wait for a job, including a finished job. Return only unseen output; waiting does not stop execution.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: send_input
tools.description: Send a line of input to a running PTY job, then wait. A missing trailing newline is added.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: kill_job
tools.description: Kill a job's process group. Go-only work is marked killed but its goroutine cannot be stopped.

tools.name: tool_limits
tools.description: Set one-shot wait/output limits for the very next call, whichever tool it is. That call reports consumption; explicit call arguments override these limits.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: micro_handoff
tools.description: Checkpoint at a completed micro-goal. Write text with what succeeded, what failed, source locations and next steps. Removes all tool traffic but preserves conversation and this note.

tools.name: keep_tool_results
tools.description: Keep the previous batch of tool results instead of automatic stubbing on supported models. Does not keep results of tools called alongside this call.

tools.name: spawn_sub_agent
tools.description: Start a full child agent with an isolated data directory. It inherits your model and restrictions; optional model selects another supported model. Children must submit results.

tools.name: join_agents
tools.description: Wait for the listed children to submit; an empty list means all children. Returns early with pending questions: answer using respond_to_parent_message, then join again. A running job report is not completion.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: agents_status
tools.description: List only your owned children and their explicit submission or failure state.

tools.name: shutdown_agent
tools.description: Stop and remove one owned child recursively. Its saved conversation remains for a later spawn with the same ID.

tools.name: send_message_to_parent
tools.description: Ask your parent (or the human for a root agent) a question and wait for a reply. This does not submit your work. If backgrounded, wait_for_job retrieves the reply.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

tools.name: respond_to_parent_message
tools.description: Answer a question sent by one of your children. Omit message_id only when that child has one pending question.

tools.name: submit
tools.description: Finish your task with a result. Rejected while children remain unfinished: join them or shut them down first.

Use run_command to run a real python3 assertion for the function after a four-second shell sleep (sleep 4 then python3). Do not create any other files, including bytecode (use python3 -B). Explicitly submit your result.

args.content:
def subtract(a, b):
    return a - b

args.command: sleep 4; python3 -B -c 'from subtract import subtract; assert subtract(7, 3) == 4; assert subtract(-7, 3) == -10; assert subtract(7, -3) == 10; assert subtract(-7, -3) == -4; assert subtract(0, 0) == 0; print("All assertions passed.")'

args.result: Created subtract.py with subtract(a, b). After sleep 4, verified positive, negative, and zero integer cases using python3 -B assertions; all passed. No children spawned or other files created.
